description: Somos a Meio Byte, um esquadrão de Engenharia da Computação especializado em encurtar a distância entre o mundo físico e o digital. Nossa força reside na versatilidade: da prototipagem de sistemas embarcados e IoT à criação de pipelines de Inteligência Artificial e aplicações em nuvem. No NASA Space Apps, nosso foco é transformar dados abertos complexos em ferramentas precisas, eficientes e automatizadas para resolver problemas globais críticos.
summary:
AstroByte bridges the gap between complex NASA data and the public by transforming technical information into accessible, engaging experiences directly on smartphones. The project offers a two-pronged approach:
 Augmented Reality (AR) Platform: A browser-based platform featuring 10 animated AR experiences, allowing users to explore concepts from the SPHEREx mission to the hypothetical Planet X.

 Space Race Educational Game: A browser-based game where players dodge asteroids and collect real stars, integrating factual information into gameplay.

How it Works (Technical Prototype)
AstroByte utilizes real NASA images and data. Python scripts generate animated 3D models incorporating NASA textures, the Tycho star map, and Kepler's laws of planetary motion. The AR experiences run directly in the mobile browser (Android and iPhone) using WebXR and AR Quick Look, supporting glTF and USDZ file formats, eliminating the need to install a dedicated app.

Key Differentiators
  Accessibility: Functions entirely within the mobile browser (iOS and Android) without requiring app installation.
 Real-time Data: Leverages real-time data from NASA.
  Educational Impact: Delivers accessible and educational content designed for all levels, combining technical accuracy with gamification.
details:
The Problem We Are Solving

The SPHEREx telescope is designed to photograph the entire sky every six months, cataloging over a billion objects and tracking how the cosmos changes over time. However, this massive amount of technical data is difficult to translate into accessible formats that can reach classrooms and the general public. For many students, the universe remains an abstract concept; they may dream of being astronauts, but they have never looked through a physical telescope.

Furthermore, educational gaps remain a significant hurdle. In Brazil, for example, students scored an average of 403 points in science on the 2022 PISA test, falling short of the OECD average of 485. Yet, there are more active smartphones in the country than inhabitants. Our goal was to bridge this gap by transforming the device already in students' hands into a powerful window to the universe.

Our Solution: AstroByte

AstroByte is a web-based educational platform that brings complex astronomical data to life through gamification and Augmented Reality (AR). We designed the platform to be entirely accessible directly from mobile browsers, requiring zero app installations. The project is divided into two core experiences:

* Augmented Reality (AR) Platform: We created 10 fully animated AR experiences. Users can project 3D models into their own physical space—exploring the SPHEREx telescope, comparing the sizes of planets, and visualizing the hypothetical orbit of Planet X.

* "Space Race" Browser Game: An interactive 2D pixel-art game where players control an astronaut, dodge asteroids, and collect "cards" containing factual information about real stars and space missions.

Technical Implementation

AstroByte was built with accessibility and scientific accuracy in mind:

* Data Processing & Modeling: We used Python to generate and animate 3D models based on real NASA images and data. Planetary movements in our models are accurately simulated using Kepler's laws of planetary motion, meaning the passage of time reflects real physics.

* Web-Native AR: To ensure cross-platform compatibility, we exported our 3D models in both glTF (for Android) and USDZ (for iPhone) formats.

* Seamless Integration: By utilizing WebXR and AR Quick Look technologies, the browser securely opens the device's camera without forcing the user to download a heavy application.

Use of Space Agency Data

AstroByte relies heavily on real astronomical data to ensure an educational experience. Our 3D models use authentic NASA textures, and our starry backgrounds are generated using the Tycho star map. The core narrative and educational content are directly inspired by the SPHEREx mission parameters (mapping the sky in 102 infrared colors every six months) and the search for Planet X.

Impact and Differentiators

AstroByte stands out because it removes the friction of traditional educational software. It works instantly on Android and iPhone browsers and uses real-time NASA data to unite technical research with gamified learning. Designed for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts of all levels, AstroByte proves that you don't need an observatory to explore the stars—the universe can fit right in the palm of your hand.
